title: Four remaining cards
observableEvidence: Counts arrangements by combining an order constraint with an adjacency exclusion and checking cases systematically.
prompt: Five cards P, Q, R, S, and T are placed in a row. P must be first, Q must appear before R, and S may not be next to T. How many rows are possible?
solutionRepresentation: With P fixed first, arrange Q, R, S, T in the remaining four positions. Half of the 24 orders have Q before R. Of those, 6 have S next to T, so 12 − 6 = 6 valid rows.
solutionMethod: Count the order-constrained arrangements, then subtract the arrangements violating the adjacency restriction.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept 6 in numeric or word form.

hintSteps.prompt: Fix the card whose position is already determined before counting anything else.
hintSteps.question: Which four cards still need to be arranged?

hintSteps.prompt: First count the orders satisfying Q before R, then identify the subset in which S and T are neighbors.
hintSteps.question: What broad count-minus-bad-cases structure fits the conditions?

hintSteps.prompt: For the bad cases, group S and T as a block in either internal order and then apply the Q-before-R condition.
hintSteps.question: How would you count the excluded neighboring cases without listing every row?

review.originalityStatement: Original card-arrangement problem written from first principles; no archive wording or arrangement is reproduced.

accessibilityNotes: Use a text list or tactile cards for the five labels; do not depend on position in a displayed graphic.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: Put P first. Arrange Q, R, S, T so Q is before R and S is not next to T. Count the rows.
